covenants.name: Interest Coverage Ratio
covenants.quote: Permit the Interest Coverage Ratio to be less than 3.00 to 1.00 for the Measurement Period ending December 31, 2025 or any Measurement Period ending thereafter.

covenants.name: Consolidated Net Leverage Ratio
covenants.quote: Permit the Consolidated Net Leverage Ratio to exceed 3.50 to 1.00 for the Measurement Period ending December 31, 2025 and any Measurement Period ending thereafter.

parsed.notes: Consolidated EBITDA adds back interest, income taxes, depreciation and amortization, and other non-cash expense (excluding accruals or reserves for future cash charges), plus certain non-cash retiree medical and pension items. It does not name stock compensation, impairments or restructuring separately, so 'other' is recorded for the general non-cash add-back. No cost-savings or synergy add-back appears. Net leverage nets domestic unrestricted cash and Cash Equivalents, plus non-domestic cash held with the Administrative Agent up to $40,000,000, with the combined netting capped at $200,000,000. The Applicable Rate pricing grid uses Consolidated Total Leverage Ratio and is not a covenant. Section 7.12 also has a 2.75x threshold limiting certain restricted payments to $75,000,000 per twelve months (Section 7.06(c)), and a 3.00x threshold limiting certain investments (Section 7.03(c)). Both are incurrence-style conditions, so they are excluded. Section 1.11 tests ratios at the signing date of a Limited Condition Acquisition, but financial covenant compliance under Section 7.12 is tested without that election. Compliance is shown in a Compliance Certificate delivered with quarterly and annual financials. A 30-day cure period applies to general covenant defaults under Section 8.01(c)(ii), but there is no equity cure.
parsed.facility: Revolving credit facilities: a $425,000,000 USD Facility and a $75,000,000 multicurrency AC Facility, both maturing November 20, 2030; sublimits include a $40,000,000 letter of credit sublimit and a $50,000,000 swing line sublimit. Up to $650,000,000 of incremental commitments are permitted. Carpenter also has $700,000,000 5.625% Senior Notes due 2034.

terms.summary: The agreement has no restriction on moving or exclusively licensing intellectual property to unrestricted subsidiaries, and it does not use an unrestricted subsidiary concept.

terms.quote: (iii) subordinate, or have the effect of subordinating, the Obligations hereunder to any other Indebtedness or other obligation; provided that, in the case of the preceding subclause (iii), only those Lenders that are directly and adversely affected thereby (without giving effect to this proviso) that have not been offered an opportunity to fund their pro rata share
terms.summary: Subordinating the loans to other debt requires consent of each directly affected lender. However, lenders who were offered their pro rata share of priming debt on the same terms can be subordinated with only Required Lender consent, so a non-pro-rata priming transaction that offers participation to all lenders may proceed.

The agreement does not say a guarantor is kept in place when it stops being wholly owned. Guarantors can be released at Carpenter's election on notice with pro forma compliance (Section 10.12(b)), and automatically when they cease to be a Subsidiary in a permitted transaction (Section 9.10(a)).

terms.quote: the aggregate amount of such Investments together with all other Investments made under this clause (iv)(B), net of all dividends, distributions, returns of capital and payments in respect of Indebtedness received after the Closing Date by the Loan Parties from any joint ventures or any Subsidiaries that are not Loan Parties, shall not exceed $75,000,000
terms.summary: Investments by Loan Parties in joint ventures or non-guarantor subsidiaries are capped at $75,000,000 net of returns, but only when the net leverage ratio is 3.00x or higher on a pro forma basis. There is no separate designation concept for unrestricted subsidiaries, and a general $10,000,000 basket applies under Section 7.03(h).
Consolidated EBITDA has no add-back for projected cost savings, synergies or restructuring, so no cap applies.
The agreement does not allow the borrower to cure a financial covenant breach with new equity. Only a 30-day grace period for general covenant defaults applies.
